scope: Host-only harness investigation. No emulator launched, no audio injected, host microphone never enabled, no physical phone. Raw logs, tokens and transcripts stay private.
question: Why did the producer read host microphone access as enabled after a lateness abort, and is there a harness defect?

protocolDefinition.microphoneState:
message MicrophoneState { // Whether or not host microphone access is enabled
 bool realAudioEnabled = 1; }
protocolDefinition.streamNotificationComment: MicrophoneState: Reports changes in the microphone state (currently whether host microphone access is allowed)
protocolDefinition.injectAudioNotes: Circular buffer ~300 ms; on stream closure writes silence for up to 300 ms; FAILED_PRECONDITION if another microphone is already active. Nothing documents the state reported during or after a cancelled stream.
protocolDefinition.versionDifference: Only an unrelated DisplayPowerModeNotification differs between 37.1.11 and 37.2.13; MicrophoneState, AudioPacket and injectAudio are identical.
protocolDefinition.meaning: Field 1 reports whether host microphone access is enabled/allowed. It is not a capture or audio-level indicator. Proto3 default false is encoded as an absent field.

survey.method: All retained parent records with a sourceProducer block under docs/reports/evidence (read-only scan)

observed: All three retained source-stream aborts were client-side realtime lateness aborts (102.9-112.7 ms over a 100 ms guard). In each, the next state read (500 ms deadline, issued right after the client cancelled the stream with RST_STREAM CANCEL) returned realAudioEnabled=true.
All 37 retained completed source streams read false afterwards; that read happens after the server finished the RPC.
Each time the producer failed closed (BLOCKED, HOST_MICROPHONE_ENABLED_AFTER_ABORT), kept the pacing code in injectionFailureReason, and reported SOURCE_RPC_ABORTED.

Each time the parent raised HOST_INPUT_NOT_CONFIRMED_DISABLED, published ABORT (never ALLOW), and the native gate recorded BLOCK_PRODUCER_ABORT with producerAuthorizedConfirmation=false; no review/Confirm ran.
The next state observation, the parent final status probe 21-25 s later after permission restoration and fixture cleanup, read OFF, OFF. No reading exists in between.

No code in scripts/ or any private helper sends setMicrophoneState; the producer issues only getMicrophoneState (empty request) and injectAudio (AudioPacket fields only); hostInputEnableRequested is never set true.
Both incidents on the original guest used the default host audio backend; null1 used -audio none (no host audio backend configured).

Windows microphone usage record (CapabilityAccessManager, read-only): the only emulator entry is the global windowed qemu-system-x86_64.exe, last used 2026-10-01 for ~2 s. There is no entry for the headless engine (global or isolated) used by every -no-window run.

Original-guest V03/2: the app capture that ended at 20:59:22.102 UTC (spanning the enabled reading) holds near-silence (rms 7.1e-05, ~-83 dBFS; energy ~2.7e-04 against ~331 for an intact fixture capture). null1 V03/2: captured energy exactly 4.000001 x the fixture energy, consistent with fixture samples plus digital zeros.
inferred: The enabled reading is tied to client cancellation of injectAudio (3/3 aborted, 0/37 completed) and is followed by OFF within <=25 s. Most consistent with emulator-side state reported while or after the cancelled injection is torn down. The mechanism is not established.
A harness enable request, parse error, stale or cross-stream response, wrong instance, or field overwrite is not supported by the code, the protocol framing or the host tests below.

Live host microphone capture is not supported by the available evidence: no host backend in null1, no Windows microphone-usage record for the headless engines, and near-silent capture in the one original-guest abort with retained capture metadata. It is not proven impossible for the two default-backend incidents.
unknown: Which component set realAudioEnabled=true, and why
How long it stayed true (bounded only by the next OFF read 21-25 s later)
Whether the emulator routed any host audio during that interval on the default-backend guest (no direct capture log for the host side)

Whether an external gRPC client (none known) could have toggled it; no host connection inventory exists for those minutes, but the 3/3 timing correlation with the harness's own cancel argues against coincidence

findings.summary: Fails closed on enabled, unknown, malformed and timed-out reads; keeps the original pacing/RPC error alongside the privacy error; never requests enablement; completed streams with a non-OFF later read are not counted as host-OFF submissions.

Its real node_audio/release_gate code blocks on every failing producer output, publishes ABORT, and a later authorization cannot replace a published ABORT; unknown after-state stays absent, never coerced to OFF.

findings.summary: Cohort rows for all three incidents record only hostMicrophoneDisabledAtEnd=true and omit the earlier enabled observation kept in the parent record. Ledgers and reports built on those rows then described host input as OFF (capture-fix report and stable report v1).
findings.fix: Historical helpers and records are retained unchanged. The current cohort helper (.local/phase08-lowload-cohort.py, frozen in the low-load plan before this investigation) carries rpc.hostMicrophoneEnabledAfter next to parent.hostMicrophoneDisabledAtEnd and stops on PRIVACY_GUARD; a regression test now locks that in. Summary corrections are recorded here and in the stable report.

findings.summary: The schema check reads the global SDK proto, not the running engine's. The relevant definitions are identical for 37.1.11/37.2.13, so the anomaly is unaffected. Not changed; binding it to the running engine is a separate decision.

After the enabled read, the app recording continued ~0.3-0.6 s until the ABORT gate released the hold; the state then went unobserved ~21-25 s until the final probe. Not changed (not a demonstrated defect); recorded as a limitation.
